title: A shifted target template gives extra blue absorption in six HD 69830 spectra under a linear shape model
abstract: We test a known HD 69830 twilight event in six public HARPS merged spectra. A template from three dark exposures is separate from the event and dark contrasts. Under a linear continuum, depth, shift and broadening model, a positive shifted target template gives its largest squared residual reduction at -5.25 km/s. The prior solar geometry gives -5.439489 km/s. At that fixed velocity, 81 of 96 wavelength blocks have positive coefficients, with a median of 0.00948. The event squared residual reduction is 1.013 percent. A dark contrast gives 50 of 96 positive coefficients and a 0.037 percent reduction. Seven sensitivity settings keep the best event velocity at -5.25 or -5.439489 km/s. This extends prior cross-correlation evidence to the merged spectrum of the same exposures. The target template is not a solar spectrum. Correlated pixels, the selected event, a linear shape model and one control night limit inference. No independent instrument confirms the source. No new planet is found. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and retrieval steps are included. Original ESO files remain external.

display.caption: The shifted secondary template improves the event contrast most near the prior solar velocity. The dark contrast has a smaller response. Coefficients are model summaries, not calibrated sky flux fractions.
